subject: Smiling Faces daycare conditional-use permit
comment: This comment is concerning the parking rule being proposed for day cares in residential areas. Being a client since before Smiling Faces moved to their new main street location from State Street, I have felt so much better taking my toddler into this new location. As you know the traffic on state street gets very heavy especially during rush hour. Pick up and drop off was more difficult for us parents as we had to merge into this congested street causing panic and uncertainty because of the many cars parked on that street. Since Smiling faces has moved to their new location on Main Street and 400 s, pick up and drop off are a breeze. I spend only 2 minutes in the parking lot to pick up and drop off. I drop off my child at 8 am where in the very spacious parking lot are only 2 more cars at the most. As I pick up my child at 430, I often find myself alone in the parking lot. To get to this facility I drive up 400 s where on that same road is Orem Elementary school. This is where I often find the most traffic on that street which effects the traffic on Main Street. Ever since the Pardo’s decided to buy this facility, surrounding neighbors have given them a rough time to settle. They don't want the day care there but let me explain why they need to expand. First at only 3 years old my daughter is starting to read. Being and elementary teacher myself, I have seen how my child has benefited from this learning center more than placing her in a normal city day care. Not only socially but academically. Second, Mrs. Pardo and her staff are certified teachers or working towards their certification. This makes this facility not a day care facility but a learning center due to its credentials. Third, as I have explained and as KSL witnessed, there is no traffic congesting either Main Street or 400 s because of Smiling Faces. Lastly, having known the Pardo’s since I was a little girl, I have always known them as kind, nurturing and upstanding citizens. They are essential to the Orem community. They have made the news with their amazing work, they have earned city awards, the mayor himself visited the facility back in the fall this year and was impressed with everything this center offers to the kids of our community. Smiling Faces should be able to expand with no difficulty. Thanks for your time.

subject: Smiling Faces daycare conditional-use permit
comment: This is regarding the 'Proposed rules pertaining to parking involving Smiling Faces Business.' German and Luz moved to Orem over 20 years ago and made it their home. They have been and are exceptional residents of the city, and upstanding citizens. They contribute positivity to the community and have always done things right. They have proved themselves as very successful business owners. At their previous location, they built their clientele by not only providing loving care for children, but an educational program as well. Helping children learn and thrive in a clean, structural, engaging, environment designed and created for the children themselves. They gained the love of each child and parent, the support of all involved in this field, as well as the city Mayor. Their hard work reflects in the many outstanding awards, and recognitions towards their program and business as a whole. Their success led to the need for their services on a larger scale, as parents begged for more enrollment openings for their children. As small business owners they decided to take a huge leap and expand, to provide for more children to benefit from their care and programs, provide the community with a greatly needed service and facilitate the life of the parents by hoping to provide easier access facilities with ample room. Their hope was set on purchasing a building which was previously a skilled facility, which was also abandoned by its previous owner, left to deteriorate on the inside and outside. It sat empty, abandoned within this 'upscale' neighborhood for years, with no plans for it in sight. Despite all the work that needed to be done to make the facilities functional, the large price tag and the endless work ahead. They made it happen. Once their interest was voiced to relocate their business to this new site, they found themselves with a much difficult challenge ahead as it was apparent that a handful of individuals were not going to make this easy for them. There seemed to be more roadblocks than realistically expected, from the most miniscule detail to expecting these owners to fund a $10,000 traffic study for the area surrounding their new building, which truly should have been something the city should have provided, funded and been on top of. They were required to personally hire an engineer to work through the new building and follow the city's guidelines for approval, they also found the need to hire a lawyer to be able to help them through the process. Despite it all, these proud business owners met every single requirement, demand and worked through every challenge thrown at them. After a very long process and much back and forth discussion and city council meetings, it was thankfully approved for them to relocate. Unfortunately after this decision they have had to endured disrespectful encounters, thoughts and comments from surrounding neighbors and even certain congressmen from the very city they have been devoted to serving and being an asset to. I have always had the hope and expectation that those in positions of authority and leadership make rational, just decisions and the ongoing resistance and lack of support towards this specific business and its owners is just dumbfounding and sad. It is challenging for me to not wonder if it would be much different were it any other business or perhaps owners. Finally, the recently spoken of 'proposed rule pertaining to parking' in this city, would not only affect first and foremost the expansion of this specific business, it will also have an impact and affect every single small and large child care business in the city of Orem and it is tough for many to find any reasonable rationale for it. Thank you!

subject: Smiling Faces daycare conditional-use permit
comment: I am an Orem citizen, please consider one or more of the alternative options: A.) Delay any vote or action until a proper traffic study has been conducted to determine impact to the neighborhood surround 410 South Main Street. B.) Grant Smiling Faces an exemption or variance to the proposed ordinance that would allow a maximum capacity of 200 students with the current parking set-up. C.) Amend the proposed ordinance so that additional parking can be provided off-site within a reasonable distance, such as across the street, so that business owners can purchase additional land to expand. D.) Amend the proposed ordinance to more accurately reflect local family child rates, so that number of parking stalls are suggested based on enrolled households and not enrolled students. Two or three children within the same home and presumably travelling together should be considered as one unit in the 0.24 scenario. Thank you for your time in looking at any combination of these ideas. Options are available to respect the homeowners that have worked hard to keep their neighborhood safe and beautiful, without completely hobbling this small business that provides an essential service to your residents. Please consider some middle ground.

subject: Smiling Faces daycare conditional-use permit
comment: My name is Chad Nichol. I’m a law enforcement officer, my Wife is a registered nurse. Throughout this pandemic where we have been on the front lines, my family has not had the luxury of working from home and staying safe, we still needed a safe environment for our two children. I have found such a safe haven in the Pardo’s amazing facility. My oldest has been going since she was born, now in second grade, she excels in her class and gets top scores, AND she is bilingual in a time where our world is changing and the need for a second language is crucial. All my thanks in this is due to the Smiling Faces Daycare and Bilingual Center. I have personally helped Mr. and Mrs. Pardo in their transition to this new building and I have personally witnessed the city putting up every road block imaginable to this poor incredible family who throughout it all, entirely insists on doing it the right way, despite the many challenges they face. I have personally witnessed the racism towards them and believe me, I don’t say that lightly. I believed in the good of people and am still at a loss for words that there is prejudice in this society, and it can come from people who are in appointed positions. I have witnessed Mr. McDonald of Orem City on multiple accounts belittle the Pardo’s. From sending emails to Mr. Pardo for having a car in the parking lot of the his own facility later in the evening (thousands of man hours has been put into restoring this building which has sat empty.), to the final straw that would support my claim of Mr. McDonalds targeting, he walked into the Pardo’s business and threatened and intimidated this amazing family. He said to Mr. Pardo “This is an upscale neighborhood and we will be motoring this place closely for any little thing that is out of place, and we will not hesitate to shut you down.” But not only did he make it a point to intimidate these hard-working Orem citizens, people he has been entrusted by, but he did it on the day of their new building’s grand opening. A day of excitement, joy and relief for the thousands of man hours and thousands upon thousands of dollars that they put into this facility to make it the safest learning environment they could. I find it odd that a key antagonist of this proposal, such as Mr. McDonald of Orem City, happens to have a son who lives in this “upscale neighborhood” very close to this wonderful business. It would seem there is a conflict of interest. He should have the ethics to withdraw himself from something where he has such a vested interest. As for the city of Orem, they should reconsider this proposal, and how it will negatively affect businesses such as the Pardo’s. I drop my kids off every morning and pick them up every afternoon and have always been the only car in the parking lot. Occasionally there has been one other car usually pulling out as I get there or pulling in as I leave. There has been no evidence of any increase in traffic due to the Pardo’s business. The Pardo’s have even spent $10,000 doing a traffic study on this subject that supports this. The city has done no investigation of their own, they have not hired an outside company to do an independent traffic study. The city needs to do their own due diligence and create unbiased results. With the ongoing pandemic, our government should be promoting small businesses that provide such a great service and are at the forefront of rebuilding our economy. We the People, trust in you. Do the right thing.
